reason: Adoption report for overlay consumers (#459, acceptance criterion 4): module-size 29687->30230 (+543), measured off e66264e. Attributed empirically, not from the arrow: per #689 the left operand of a check-arch verdict is baselines.json (26965, stale -- tracked in #703) and every allowance merged since it was refreshed sits inside that gap, so the real base was obtained by removing the feat-462 allowance and re-running `harness check-arch --json` on the untouched branch point (29687, six under that allowance's 29693). Moving ts/src/core/adoption.ts aside and re-running gives 29740, so the one new module is 490 of the 543 and the two call-site edits (ts/src/cli.ts option, ts/src/cli-commands.ts dispatch) are the remaining 53. Nothing else in the diff contributes: ts/test/adoption.test.ts and the five new ts/test/canary-migrate-cli.test.ts cases are test code and module-size does not count them, and the rest is CHANGELOG.md and docs/guides/tracked-overlays.md. The growth buys the one acceptance criterion #459 still had open. The install half (shape-aware, portable paths, idempotent, never-clobber) shipped in v6.3.0 via #484; what was missing was a way to SEE a half-finished adoption, which is the failure the issue actually reports -- overlay skills present, no workflow installed, guardian never runs, every surface green. Of the 490 lines roughly 190 are comment and doc block, deliberately, because four of this module's choices are ones a later reader would otherwise reverse: it lives in the engine rather than in `canary doctor` (doctor is in the CommonJS npm shim, which structurally cannot import the ESM engine -- the same boundary sync-gate-result.mjs exists for -- and every piece reported here is an engine concept, so keeping it in doctor would mean a second implementation of shape detection, the thing most likely to drift); a workflow that differs from the template is `present`, not a gap, because a consumer's CI is theirs (#459's recorded decision) and nagging about hand-tuned CI would be worse than the partial adoption being reported; an undeclared path pointer is `unknown` rather than `missing`, because a template with no pointer falls back to its own default and whether that default fits the repo is not knowable from the repo -- calling it a gap would raise a finding against every correctly-working lcov-default consumer; and the report runs WITHOUT an overlay, because 'no overlay is tracked' is itself the most common gap and refusing to report until one exists would hide it. Splitting would not help -- module-size is a repo-wide aggregate, so N files summing to 543 score identically to one, and the file is well under every per-file threshold. Nothing was absorbed here to avoid a fix: newViolations is 0 and the pre-existing threshold violations went DOWN, 21 to 20. Folding both report-only modes into one `migrateReportOnly` dispatch retired migrateCmd's pre-existing cyclomaticComplexity=18 finding instead of growing it, which is why the adoption branch cost migrateCmd nothing. Entropy is 280 against a 291 ceiling -- exactly the branch point's 280, a delta of zero -- because both new exports have real callers (`gatherAdoptionReport` from ts/src/cli-commands.ts, `buildAdoptionReport` from the unit suite via the gatherer). No entropy entry point was declared (the module is reachable from the existing ts/src/cli.ts entry point) and maxFindings was not touched.
